content: 1. Omeprazole and CYP3A4 Substrates: Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered when co-administered with omeprazole. 2. Omeprazole and Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Omeprazole decreases the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir due to its effect on gastric pH. Ledipasvir's solubility decreases as pH increases. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) like omeprazole (≤20 mg) can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. 3. Omeprazole and Lemborexant: Omeprazole increases lemborexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 4. Letermovir and Omeprazole: Letermovir increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and potential dose adjustments may be necessary. 5. Omeprazole and Lomitapide: Omeprazole increases lomitapide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 6. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor and Omeprazole: Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 enzymes. Monitor closely for reduced omeprazole efficacy. 7. Omeprazole and Methotrexate: Omeprazole increases methotrexate levels by reducing renal clearance. Temporary withdrawal of PPIs may be considered in some patients. 8. Omeprazole and Methylphenidate: Omeprazole decreases the effects of methylphenidate by altering its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies to the oral forms of both agents. Consider separating the administration of antacids or acid suppressants from methylphenidate extended-release capsules. 9. Omeprazole and Midazolam (Intranasal): Omeprazole increases midazolam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially prolonging sedation. Monitor closely. 10. Modafinil and Omeprazole: Modafinil increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Omeprazole and Mycophenolate: Omeprazole decreases mycophenolate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies to the oral forms of both agents. Enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium is less sensitive to this interaction. 12. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir and Dasabuvir with Omeprazole: These agents decrease omeprazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor for reduced omeprazole efficacy and consider dose adjustments. 13. Omeprazole and Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor closely. 14. Omeprazole and Pentobarbital/Phenobarbital: Both drugs decrease omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Omeprazole and Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 16. Omeprazole and Polysaccharide Iron: Omeprazole decreases iron absorption by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies to oral forms of both agents. 17. Omeprazole and Posaconazole: Omeprazole decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH, while posaconazole increases omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 18. Omeprazole and Primidone: Primidone decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Omeprazole and Rifampin: Rifampin decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Omeprazole and Riociguat: Omeprazole decreases riociguat levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies to oral forms of both agents. 21. Omeprazole and Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Omeprazole and Rose Hips: Omeprazole decreases the effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies to oral forms of both agents. 23. Omeprazole and Sparsentan: Sparsentan decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor closely. 24. Omeprazole and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Omeprazole and Stiripentol: Stiripentol increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions occur. 26. Omeprazole and Tacrolimus: Omeprazole increases tacrolimus levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor tacrolimus blood concentrations, especially in intermediate or poor CYP2C19 metabolizers. 27. Omeprazole and Tazemetostat: Omeprazole increases tazemetostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Omeprazole and Tinidazole: Omeprazole increases tinidazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Omeprazole and Tofacitinib: Omeprazole increases tofacitinib levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. No specific dose adjustment is recommended unless co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 30. Omeprazole and Triclabendazole: Triclabendazole increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Omeprazole and Vismodegib: Omeprazole decreases vismodegib levels by increasing gastric pH, potentially reducing bioavailability. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Omeprazole and Voriconazole: Voriconazole increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 33. Omeprazole and Warfarin: Omeprazole increases warfarin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust warfarin dose as needed. 34. Omeprazole and Acetazolamide: Acetazolamide increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 35. Omeprazole and Alprazolam: Omeprazole increases alprazolam levels by decreasing metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Omeprazole and Ambrisentan: Omeprazole increases ambrisentan levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Omeprazole and Anastrozole: Anastrozole increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 38. Omeprazole and Bismuth Subsalicylate: Omeprazole increases bismuth subsalicylate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Omeprazole and Blessed Thistle: Blessed thistle decreases omeprazole effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This is a theoretical interaction. 40. Omeprazole and Bosentan: Bosentan decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Omeprazole and Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. 42. Omeprazole and Cefpodoxime/Cefuroxime: Omeprazole decreases the effects of these antibiotics by increasing gastric pH. Monitor closely. 43. Omeprazole and Cannabidiol: Omeprazole increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor closely and consider dose adjustments. 44. Omeprazole and Capecitabine: Omeprazole decreases capecitabine effects by impairing tablet dissolution and absorption due to elevated gastric pH. Monitor closely. 45. Omeprazole and Citalopram: Omeprazole increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Limit citalopram to 20 mg/day to reduce the risk of QT prolongation. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when omeprazole is co-administered with other medications, particularly those metabolized by CYP enzymes or affected by changes in gastric pH.
